articleTitle: A Full-Dimensional Robot Teleoperation Platform
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: In general, robot teleoperation system is conducted through either joysticks or game pads. Due to the requirement for the robot to function in several degrees of freedom, the system is usually complex and the users must be well trained to operate them (e.g., tilting the joystick to the left for rotating the robot to the right). To address this challenge, a full-dimensional infrared-matrix-based immersive robot teleoperation platform is proposed for users to program and control robots. The developed platform enables humans to manipulate specific parts of the robot directly through touching the corresponding component on the interface. The system can therefore provide intuitive operation allowing users to program and maneuver the robot with minimal training and even without robotics expertise. We describe the details of the hardware and software system implementation. In addition, we conduct two kinds of experiments for robot controlling according to user interaction in real-world human-robot collaboration contexts. Experimental results suggest that the developed platform can effectively assist humans in robot programming and operation without coding effort required.

articleTitle: Optimization of Electric Vehicle Battery Size and Reduction Ratio Using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: A battery electric vehicle (BEV), known as a pure electric vehicle, exclusively uses chemical energy stored in rechargeable battery units (BUs), with no secondary source of propulsion. In this study a genetic algorithm (GA) based optimization study has been performed in order to find the optimum battery size or capacity and the final drive ratio (FDR) for the given driving profiles of an electric vehicle to find maximum range and minimum acceleration time for a BEV. Numerous startups and conventional automotive companies offer a variety of electric vehicles to customers from small electric motorcycles to full-size passenger vehicles. Battery sizing is very critical as it is the main factor for driving range. However excessive battery allocation will increase vehicle cost and weight significantly. Optimized input parameters of FDR and battery capacity were calculated to obtain maximum value of composite objective function which requires maximization of range and minimization of acceleration time of the vehicle at the same time, in the given interval of input parameters.

articleTitle: Computational Study of Noise Reduction in CFM56-5B Using Core Nozzle Chevrons
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: Computational investigations of noise reduction in the CFM56-5B engine were carried out using optimal core nozzle chevron configurations. Two types of chevron designs were considered for the study, i.e. conventional triangular chevrons and rounded chevrons. Smooth edges instead of conventional pointed sharp edges were introduced in the rounded chevron design. Multiple chevron configurations were used for the analysis and noise reduction results of the two chevron types were compared with the noise generation values of the core nozzle (without chevrons). Both types of chevron design successfully reduced noise levels; however, the noise mitigation was more significant in the case of smooth-edged rounded chevrons which demonstrated noise reduction of more than 10% of the overall noise generated at the engine core nozzle. Smooth-edged rounded chevrons can be a good choice for the future noise reduction studies of CFM 56 engine series.

articleTitle: Development of Intelligent Door Locking System Based on Face Recognition Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost smart door locking system capable of making decisions based on facial recognition technology. The system operates through a combination of Arduino UNO and Android-based smartphone. It is capable of performing all the facial recognition stages on its own such as face detection, features extraction, face recognition applying OpenCV libraries. The identification is fast and non-contact, providing an increase in comfort for system users. Moreover, the system has a secondary protection level, such as the conventional pin-code based and RFID based security levels that extend the functionality. The main advantage of the system is its autonomous function; once the system is installed, there is no need to supervise it. The system is easy to tune, and the Android OS allows to update the database for face recognition easily.

articleTitle: A Simplified Design Approach for High-Speed Wind Tunnels. Part-I.I: Optimized Design of Settling Chamber and Inlet Nozzle
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: This study was carried out after the initial divergent nozzle contours of the high-speed wind tunnel inlet nozzle were designed in [1]. The goal of the study is to design a suitable and simplified inlet section (settling chamber, C-D nozzle, and test section) of the supersonic wind tunnel prototype. At first, an optimized design for the settling chamber was created after which the settling chamber could be used for any planned Mach configuration (1.5≤M≤3). In the next step, three different designs for the inlet section of the wind tunnel were created and a suitable design for the future manufacturing of the inlet section was selected with the help of the numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Dynamic Identification of Nozzle Throat Diameter of a Solid Rocket Motor and Experimental Validation based on Micron-CT 3D Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: Currently, some necessary material performance parameters and accurate numerical simulation boundary can hardly be obtained via numerical analysis of the ablation laws of the solid rocket motor throat. Based on throat diameter dynamic identification and micron-CT 3D scanning reconstruction technique, the nozzle throat diameters of three types of SRM during the operating phase were dynamically identified, the throat before and after the test was reconstructed via 3D scanning and the static throat diameter change was analyzed. The results demonstrate that throat diameter dynamic identification technique in this study exhibits higher precision than micron-CT three-dimensional reconstruction, with a maximum error of only 0.327%. The negative ablation phenomenon appeared in the test can be attributed to the deposition of Al2O3 particulate-phase. Overall, the proposed method exhibits remarkable engineering application values and promotion significance.

articleTitle: Tensile Behaviour of a 3D Printed Lattice Structure
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: An additive technology can produce complex geometries which might not have been possible to produce using traditional manufacturing techniques. One such geometry is a lattice structure that can lighten the core of a component. The article deals with the investigation of tensile properties of the samples made from ABS (Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene) material. Two types of cylindrical lightened samples (with a simple lattice structure and in the form of a tube) were analyzed experimentally. FDM (Fused Deposition modelling) technique and filament of a 1.7 mm diameter were selected for the samples production. The results showed that at almost the same cross-section area of the samples, the lattice structure can carry a higher tensile yield strength compared with a shelled tube sample.

articleTitle: The Performance Simulation for A Gear Pump by Trapped Oil Model
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: A trapped oil model of a gear pump with relief groove is given and its performance is simulated. First, the main geometrical parameters are confirmed. Furthermore, the three-dimensional model of the gear pump is completed by CAD. Then, the trapped oil model is established by analyzing the process of gear pump oil trapping, where the trapped oil flow and volume are calculated and the basic quantity is solved. Finally, the performances for different leakages are simulated by using the trapped oil model. The results show that the gear pump's axial clearance leakage, meshing leakage, side clearance leakage and unloading leakage are all reproduced, which is consistent with expectations. The obtained conclusions have a certain engineering practical significance for the design and simulation research of high-performance gear pumps.

articleTitle: Research on the Design of Electromagnetic Environment EMC Evaluation System for Aviation Station
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: Based on the analysis and research of the electromagnetic environment compatibility of airport and air station, a system for evaluating the electromagnetic environment compatibility of airport and air station is designed according to the civil aviation operation specifications and requirements. It focuses on the overlapping coverage between the navigation station and the navigation station, the influence of the ground environment on the distribution of electromagnetic signals, the shielding effect of typical obstacles on electromagnetic signals, and the interference of main interference sources on the electromagnetic environment The contents of the evaluation are as follows: to establish the radiation interference evaluation model; to visualize the electromagnetic signal distribution and interference sources of the air station, so as to effectively evaluate the electromagnetic environment around the civil aviation airport and the air station, and to provide an intuitive reference for the design of the electromagnetic protection zone.

articleTitle: Longitudinal Flying Qualities Evaluation Method for Receiver in Probe and Drogue Aerial Refueling
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: The receiver aircraft needs to have the ability to accurately track the flight path during the probe and drogue aerial refueling, but the conventional military flying qualities standards are insufficient. In this paper, a man-machine closed-loop system for the probe and drogue refueling task is established, and a digital virtual flight simulation method is used to simulate closed-loop tracking tasks. Based on the task-dependent handling-quality metric derived by simulation results, the pilot's perception of task difficulty is evaluated, so as to reflect the flying qualities of the receiver to track the flight path. By comparing the handling-quality metric with the Cooper-Harper rating obtained from the mission-based human-in-the-loop flight test, quantitative requirements for handling-quality metric are proposed. The conclusions can provide important theoretical reference for the design of flight control laws for the probe and drogue refueling mode and the simulation method proposed in this paper has an extensive application prospect in the prediction of flying qualities.

articleTitle: Modal Analysis and Experimental Plan of Thin-Walled Workpieces in Turning Cutting Process
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: In a machining process, self excited vibrations (chatter) take an important place in many research works. In classic cases, with a massive workpieces, chatter vibrations occur when the depth of cut or the cutting speed exceeds the stability of machine tool. But with a thin wall workpiece, the situation of chatter vibration problems is not so simple. Thus, the main object of our study is to qualify the dynamic behaviour of a thin walled workpieces during a turning cutting process. In this part of our study, we will present some results of a modal analysis, calculated with a finite element program on tubular workpieces with different materials (steel, aluminium and titanium alloys) and with several geometry and setting parameters. The mode frequencies are then analyzed with Yats factorial experimental plan (3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) to define and make in evidence the main controlled design factors.

articleTitle: Generative Design of the Roller Seat of the Wind Turbine Blade Turnover Machine Based on Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: Generative design is a design exploration technology based on an artificial intelligence algorithm. By constraining the manufacturing process and product performance requirements, generative design can generate a variety of feasible models in cloud computing. In this paper, according to the load condition of the roller seat of the wind turbine blade turnover machine, several models that meet the design requirements are generated by using the generative design. After analyzing and comparing several models, the best model is obtained. Next, the structural strength and stiffness of the new model are simulated and analyzed. Compared with the parameters of the original model, the stress distribution of the new model generated by the generative design is uniform, the maximum displacement is reduced from 0.138mm to 0.126mm, and the mass is only 44.4% of the original model.

articleTitle: Actuator Fault Diagnosis of an Aero-Engine Based on Unknown Input Observers
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: An aero-engine is an aerodynamic thermal system, which has complex mechanical structure and corresponding control structure. To ensure the reliability and stability of an aero-engine, accurate and effective fault diagnosis is required. In this paper, actuator fault diagnosis of an aero-engine is studied. Unknown input observers (UIOs) are proposed for different types of actuator faults, so the residual set can be obtained, which contains fault information, realizing actuator fault diagnosis. The results show that, the UIOs proposed in this paper can effectively decouple the actuator faults, showing strong robustness. Then, achieve fault detection and isolation, reflecting the accuracy and timeliness of fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Aluminum Combustion in Solid Propellant by Using Photomicrography and Digital In-Line Holography
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: Aluminum (Al) combustion is an important research area for improving the performance of solid propellants. During the combustion of the solid propellant, aluminum particles can form large-sized agglomerates that may result in poor combustion performance, losses of two-phase flow and even affects the combustion stability of solid rocket motors. Therefore, to obtain the combustion characteristics of aluminum particles in solid propellants is of great importance. Due to the complex combustion environment of solid propellants, diagnostics of dynamic combustion process of aluminum particle are difficult. A few measurement methods can be used. In order to study the combustion characteristics of aluminum particles, photomicrography and digital in-line holography are proposed for the research in this paper. In current work, a combustor was used for the combustion experimental of solid propellants under atmospheric pressure. In addition, an optical system was constructed to diagnose the dynamic combustion process of aluminum particles. Base on this optical system, photomicrography and digital in-line holography were successfully applied to the dynamic combustion diagnosis of aluminum particles. From microscopic images, the dynamic processes of accumulation, aggregation and agglomeration of aluminum particles on the burning surface were captured, some detailed movement processes were analyzed. Considering the limitation of the depth of field in photomicrography method, digital in-line holography was used to obtain the dynamic combustion process of aluminum particles in the plume. The results show that both methods can capture the dynamic combustion process of aluminum particles. The three stages of agglomerate formation on the burning surface were obtained clearly, and the second mergence process of agglomerates was also captured. In general, the methods proposed in this paper can be effectively used in the study of aluminum combustion and provide more useful data for establishment of aluminum combustion model.

articleTitle: Optimization Methodology for Lithium-Ion Battery Temperature Sensor Placement Based on Thermal Management and Thermal Runaway Requirement
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: The layout of temperature sensors mainly designed for the requirement of thermal management. The acquisition of temperature rise of lithium-ion battery is to get the condition for cooling on. However, in some extreme cases, the placed temperature sensors can not detect the precursor of thermal runaway of a specific cell. The objective of this paper is to optimize the temperature sensor placement to satisfy both thermal management and thermal runaway requirement. To achieve the goal, The temperature sensors placement of lithium-ion battery module was analyzed under charging and discharging conditions for thermal management requirement. Then, the temperature distribution of battery module was studied considering thermal runaway and the optimization results of temperature sensors placement was given. The temperature signal of the cell experiencing thermal runaway can be detected by the neighboring cell. In order to satisfy the requirement for thermal management and thermal runaway, one temperature sensor is placed every two cells on the middle part of the cell and two temperature sensors are placed on the upper part of the side cells.

articleTitle: Dynamics of Space Tether System in Circular Orbit in Presence of Aerodynamic Drag
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: Space tether system is a promising technology that can be applied to solve many practical problems of astronautics. This work is devoted to the study of a space tether system dynamics under the influence of the atmosphere on end bodies. An original approximation of the atmosphere density is proposed. This approximation allows to obtain a new analytical solution describing the space tether oscillations. The stationary equilibrium positions of the system are found. The problem of the space tether system spin-up using aerodynamic drag is considered as an example of applying the obtained solution. It is proposed to put the system into rotation mode by inflating a large cross-section balloon at its lower end. An analytical expression that determines the required balloon cross-sectional area is obtained. Numerical simulation confirms the correctness of the analytical result.

articleTitle: Research on Formation Mechanism and Behavior Control of Adiabatic Shear of Hard Turning Die Steel
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: Based on the analysis of the construction of hard turning geometric model by Third Wave Advantedge system, with the help of hard turning experiments, the influence of the change of cutting speed, feed rate, and cutting depth on chip morphology in the cutting process is analyzed. Then the formation mechanism of serrated chips in hard turning is systematically studied, which provides theoretical support for optimizing the cutting parameters and guiding the actual production. Based on the analysis of temperature, stress, and strain rate during hard turning, this article study the adiabatic shear behavior and chip formation mechanism of hard turning in detail, and the active control of sawtooth chip formation by adiabatic shear in hard turning is characterized.

articleTitle: Aero-engine Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: For aero-engines, bearing fault monitoring and diagnosis can greatly improve its reliability. Based on the successful application of deep learning algorithms in the mapping of complex nonlinear systems, this paper proposes an aero-engine bearing fault diagnosis method that combines convolutional neural networks and support vector machine. Firstly, the Short-time Fourier transform is used to perform time-frequency analysis on time series signals (including nine faults and one normal) to obtain corresponding time-frequency images. Then, the convolutional neural network is used to extract the feature of the obtained time-frequency images. Furthermore, the support vector machine is used to classify and diagnose the faults from the extracted feature. Finally, based on the data set of Case Western Reserve University, the feasibility is validated. The results show that the proposed method has achieved a bearing fault recognition rate of more than 99%, which can effectively complete the fault diagnosis task.

articleTitle: Aeroengine Gain-Scheduling Control Based on Performance Degradation with Constrained Control Inputs
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: This paper develops a new gain-scheduling control based on performance degradation with constrained control inputs for aeroengine with strong nonlinearity. This is accomplished by constructing an improved on-board adaptive aeroengine model to estimate engine performance degradation. Meanwhile, multiple operating points are selected in the flight envelope of the engine and the controllers under engine normal state and performance degradation state at these operating points are designed and scheduled by scheduling parameter and health parameters to control the plant. Simulation results show that the developed gain-scheduling controller can be used effectively to control a degraded turbofan engine for large thrust commands, with guaranteed stability and proper tracking performance.

articleTitle: Controller Design Using SDRE Method for Tilt-Wing UAV
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: This paper proposes the flight controller for quad tilt-wing (QTW) UAV during transition flight. QTW-UAV is unstable during transition flight because the dynamic behavior of QTW-UAV exhibits nonlinearity significantly by the change of wing angle. Hence, it is necessary to design the flight controller that guarantees stability under a situation to exist high nonlinearity. The state-dependent Riccati equation (SDRE) control method is one of the solutions of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation when considering nonlinear optimal control problems. The SDRE control method calculates control inputs every control cycle to solve a nonlinear optimal regulation problem. Therefore, this method can design the control system to deal with the change of the wing angle. The effectiveness of the proposed method is shown by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: A Numerical Study on the Influence of the Rear Wing Size on the Thrust Performance of the Two Dimensional Tandem Flapping Wings
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: In this paper, the thrust performance of the two-dimensional elliptic tandem flapping wings is numerically investigated on five different rear wings of chord length varying between 0.5C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> to 1.5C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> at an interval 0.25C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>. Here, C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> is the chord length of the front wing that is kept constant. The aspect ratio (i.e. the ratio of the chord length and thickness of the wing) of all the wing is fixed as 8. The Strouhal number and Reynolds number based on the chord length of the front wing is set as 0.32 and 5000, respectively. The starting phase angle between the two wings is maintained at 0 deg for in-phase flapping. It is found that the identical rear wings in a tandem flapping mode (in the presence of front wing) produce a significantly large amount of thrust force as compared to in a single flapping mode (in the absence of front wing). From the thorough investigation of the flow regime and vortex structure, it is observed that the constructive interaction of the shear layers of the front wing and the leading edge vortex of the rear wing results in higher thrust performance in tandem flapping mode. The transient peak thrust is noticed for the rear wing having the smallest size. The correlation of the flow regime and transient thrust coefficient is also discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Optimization Problems of Crash-Resistant Fuel Systems Design Calculations for Helicopters Using Mathematical Modeling
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: At the design stage of fuel systems there are widely applied one-dimensional mathematical simulations software complexes that replace the real complex systems and structures with block diagrams as mathematical blocks models that fully describe these systems and structures. Significant limitation of one-dimensional mathematical models leads to inability for correct calculation of the spatial distribution of selected parameters considering geometric features of system structural components. This limitation does not allow conduct search and optimization studies for several operating conditions of the fuel system. This article proposes a methodology for creating a complex mathematical model of the fuel system that allows for the calculation of characteristics considering their spatial distribution. The methodology is based on the joint work of one-dimensional and three-dimensional mathematical models as a single calculation complex.

articleTitle: An Efficient Method for Non-uniform Solid Rocket Motor Grain Burnback Simulation
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: We proposed a Minimum Travel Time Method (MTTM) to perform burnback simulation of non-uniform solid rocket motor grains. The innovative method builds a mathematic model to calculate minimum travel time field of flame front. The field describes geometry of burning surface at any time in the form of isosurface. Test results show that the method provides accurate prediction for non-uniform grains. Parallel computing technology can be easily applied to accelerate MTTM, and achieve much higher performance than general graphic methods.

articleTitle: Dynamic Characteristics Determination and Optimization of Marine Engine Foundation
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: In this study structural analysis following by modal analysis of marine engine has been performed. Initially the engine foundation made of steel was modeled in Creo software and then it was imported to ANSYS for structural and vibrational analysis. During structural analysis failure analysis while modeshapes were analyzed during vibrational analysis. The foundation was designed as per the equipment manufacture guidelines. Similarly different commercially available sizes of I-beams were considered for analysis and optimization of foundation. Thicknesses of flanges and webs of I-beams were varied in order to check the effect on frequency variation and structural failure. Purpose was to obtain the optimized and resonant free structure. Moreover the results were consequently correlated with MATLAB PDE module results. Both the software's results were found in close agreement with each other. Similarly concept of composite foundation was introduced for further reduction in weight as an alternate and light weight solution. For the purpose highly resistive against loss in its properties polymer, Poly Ether Ether Ketone (PEEK) was selected and analyzed. Different combination of stacking were applied and consequently optimized, safer and alternate solution was obtained successfully.

articleTitle: A Study on Coupling Dynamics of Satellite Antenna System Considering Joint Clearances and Flexible Reflector
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: In this work, the dynamics responses of satellite antenna system considering joint clearances and flexible reflection are investigated using a computational method. Clearances are always existence in joints of the driving and positioning mechanism of the satellite antenna system. Considering clearance in joint, the contact force model of clearance joint is established using a nonlinear continuous contact force model and the friction effect is considered by a modified Coulomb friction model. The antenna reflection is considered as flexible body and it is modelled by modal expansion method. Then, a satellite antenna driven by dual-axis driving and positioning mechanism is used as the application example. The numerical simulation of satellite antenna system with clearance joints and flexible reflection is presented. Finally, the coupling dynamic characteristics of satellite antenna considering clearances and flexible reflection are discussed and analyzed.

articleTitle: A Robust Re-configurable Quad-Rotor for One Engine Inoperative Conditions
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: This work presents a specific class of quad-rotors that can effectively addresses the problem of One-Engine-Inoperative condition (OEI). The proposed quad belongs to the class of Re-Configurable Quadrotors (ReCoQu) that are equipped with Variable-Positioning Arms. This special feature makes it a fail-safe system for cases where One Engine becomes Inoperative (OEI). This feature is crucial for those quads that are expected to operate over cities and populated areas. The proposed design accounts for any change in moments of inertia and reacts accordingly. Having an extra degree-of-freedom (changing angles between arms) in the ReCoQu is the key to its resilience to disturbances similar to the one occurs during OEI condition. This feature allows a ReCoQu to assume a stable configuration, whenever necessary. This work demonstrates various configurations to maintain a stable flight even during OEI conditions. In fact, with the help of proper sensors, the ReCoQu identifies the inoperative engine and quickly reconfigures itself to allow safe maneuvers, including landing. Further investigation is necessary for the cases of multiple engine failures.

articleTitle: Homogenization of V-pattern Folded Core Sandwich Panels Using Finite Element Simulations
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: A finite element based homogenization approach is presented and adopted to predict the equivalent stiffness properties for V-pattern folded core sandwich panels. Due to the inherent periodic feature of the V-pattern folded core sandwich panel, one single unit cell was studied and periodic boundary conditions were imposed so as to obtain the in-plane, coupling and bending stiffness properties. Furthermore, influence of transverse shear deformation was considered. The first order shear deformation theory was used together with a finite element simulation for a three-dimensional (3-D) folded core sandwich beam model to derive the transverse shear stiffness. Then a comparative study between the detailed 3-D V-pattern folded core sandwich panel and corresponding two-dimensional (2-D) equivalent plate model was performed and the deflection results were compared. The results show that the transverse shear influence should not be neglected for a V-pattern folded core sandwich panel subjected to a transverse load. The homogenized 2-D plate model predicts deformations with satisfactory accuracy when the transverse shear stiffness is included.

articleTitle: Large Eddy Simulation of the Effects of Swirl and Bluff Body on Premixed Flame
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: Based on OpenFOAM, the large eddy simulation of the reaction flow field of Cambridge Stratified Swirl Burner under different swirl intensity was carried out. The finite rate model PaSR was used for combustion simulation, and the two-step reaction mechanism was optimized based on the simplified rate parameters of GRI-Mech3.0. The results show that the simulation results can accurately predict the average axial velocity and the average circumferential velocity distribution. The swirl intensity has important effects on the reaction flow field. With the increase of swirl intensity, the position of the backflow zone behind the bluff body moves away from the bluff body, and the turbulence of the flame front of instantaneous temperature increases. The large-scale coherent structure near the shear layer was shown by Q-criterion. It is found that the position of vortex breaking moves towards the blunt body with the increase of swirl intensity.

articleTitle: Heat Exchanger Design Optimization Using Mathematical Modeling Methods for Selective Laser Sintering of Metal Powder
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: One of the key components of modern aircraft is a complex of airborne systems. A complex of on-board systems is a combination of interconnected systems, including a hydraulic system, an aircraft remote control system, an air conditioning system, etc., ensuring the performance of the aircraft's target functions. The complex of on-board systems includes many units that ensure reliable and trouble-free operation of the aircraft. For modern aircraft, helicopter and space technology, the issue of ensuring thermal balance is one of the main ones. Heat exchangers (HE) are widely used in the aviation and space industries. Such devices are used to ensure and maintain a given temperature regime by removing or supplying energy in relation to the working area. [1, 2] In general, a HE is a device for communicating energy from a heated coolant to a colder one. The effectiveness of HE depends on many factors, priority is:- heat transfer coefficient characterizing the proportion of transferred heat;- design features of the HE.To improve the characteristics of heat exchangers, technologies are actively developing to create highly efficient and reliable HE designs. The most optimal method of manufacturing the apparatus is laser sintering of a metal powder. Additive technologies allow you to produce parts directly from a computer file containing a 3D model. And this, in turn, provides flexibility that allows the rapid production of complex customized products and spare parts, which either cannot be manufactured using traditional production technologies or are required in small volumes.

articleTitle: Research on 7050-T7451 Shear Angle Correction Model Based on Anisotropic Features
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: With Oxley orthogonal cutting experiments, cutting parameters such as cutting force and shear angle are obtained according to the anisotropic characteristics of the material. A constitutive model of aluminum alloy 7050-T7451 was constructed by using the Split-Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) dynamic compression test and the inverse method to introduce the spatial angle. The high-speed cutting finite element simulation was performed based on the finite element DEFORM software. The shear angle obtained by Buda criterion is compared with that obtained by traditional shear angle model and simulation. The result showed that the shear angle decreases first and then increases as the forming angle increases. Based on the comparison error, the traditional shear angle model was modified, and a shear angle model capable of fully characterizing the anisotropy of aviation aluminum alloy 7050-T7451 was obtained.

articleTitle: Research on the Elastoplastic Properties of Auxetic Honeycombs under Tensile Load
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: The auxetic honeycomb core exhibits geometric nonlinearity under the in-plane load. As the load increases, the plastic deformation occurs. The elastoplastic model of the auxetic honeycombs with constant wall thickness is introduced based on nonlinear beam theory and elastoplastic theory. The solution algorithm is established. The elastoplastic properties of the auxetic honeycombs with different ratios of the thickness of honeycomb wall to the length of the inclined wall t/l, different ratios of the height of the vertical wall to the length of the inclined wall h/l, and different inclination angle θ are obtained. The results suggest that with the increase of strain, the geometric nonlinearity causes the overall stiffness of honeycombs to increase. Then it decreases gradually due to the plastic deformation.

articleTitle: Multiple Model-Based Hybrid Kalman Filter for Fault Diagnosis of Jet Engines
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: This paper studies a multi-model-based hybrid Kalman filter fault diagnosis method. This method uses a non-linear airborne model to adapt to the level of engine degradation, and uses probability density functions to perform hypothesis testing. It can effectively solve the problem of threshold selection and evaluation. The paper establishes the working state model of aero engine. By analyzing various fault situations of sensors, components and actuators, fault-free filters and filter banks of sensors, components and actuators are constructed. By using a Gaussian density function recursive algorithm to locate the fault, the credibility ranking of the fault occurrence site is generated to achieve the purpose of fault isolation. Simulation results show that the algorithm can achieve effective detection and isolation of aero-engine gas path faults, and meet the real-time requirements of airborne computers.

articleTitle: A Rapid Exploration Method of Equivalence Ratio for the Valveless Pulse Detonation Rocket Engine
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: The equivalence ratio is a key parameter for the stable operation of the valveless pulse detonation rocket engine. In this paper, a rapid exploration method of equivalence ratio is proposed, which improves the efficiency and adaptability of equivalence ratio and make a promotion to the research process of valveless pulse detonation rocket engine.

articleTitle: Study on Serrated Chip Formation of Aluminum Alloy 7050-T7451 in Ultra-high-Speed Cutting
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: In this paper, aluminum alloy (AA) 7050-T7451 was taken as the research object and the high-speed right-angle cutting simulation model was adopted to simulate the cutting process under different cutting speeds (1000-4000 m/min) and feed rates. Besides, the chip formation law was analyzed under different cutting parameters. The simulation results were validated by experiments and it showed that simulation had high reliability. Moreover, the chip formation was predicted by ultra-high-speed (4000-6000 m/min) cutting simulation. It was discovered that the sawtooth degree and sawtooth frequency increased with the increase of cutting speed. When cutting speed was 1000-4000 m/min, the sawtooth degree increased with the increase of feed rate. However, when cutting speed exceeded 2513 m/min, the sawtooth degree was affected by cutting thickness, which made the sawtooth degree decrease with the increase of feed rate. The critical cutting speed of serrated chip formation was 1257 m/min. When the critical speed reached 6000 m/min, the sawtooth degree was close to 1. The chip shape changed from serrated to cracked, it implied that the chip transformed from plastic to brittle under this speed.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Turbulence Model Effects on Heat Flux Prediction in Opposing Jet Flowfields
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: An investigation about the turbulence model effects of computational fluid dynamic predictions of the heat flux on a blunt-body model surface with a sonic opposing jet issuing into supersonic crossflow is presented. The simulations are implemented by solving Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes, RANS equations with 6 different turbulence models. Current numerical results are compared with the reference experimental results. It is found that the predicted heat flux profiles and heat load results are highly dependent on the turbulence model. The k-ω based model show relatively preferable performance and the realizable k-ω model is the most qualified. The flowfield results indicate that the recirculation regions forming around the jet exit play a crucial role in the heat reduction of the model. The k-ε based models and SA model underestimate the length of the region and the heat flux peak value resulting in a large error.

articleTitle: Air Pressure Reducer Characteristics Research and Simulation Verification
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: The air pressure reducer belongs to the control accessory of the aero-engine. It mainly senses the pressure drop ratio of the turbine and adjusts it by the anti-pressure action of the internal flow channel. This paper analyzes the working characteristics of the air pressure reducer. The four working sections of the pressure reducer were proved by theory. The relationship between the structural parameters of the pressure reducer and the performance of the pressure reduction ratio was found, which provided a theoretical basis for the manufacture and use of the pressure reducer. In order to make the theoretical conclusions of this paper more convincing, this paper also uses CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) to simulate the pressure reducer model. The simulation results show that the theoretical results are correct and reliable.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of the No-bleed Air Conditioning System for an Advanced Passenger Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: At the moment, the most perspective development direction of the aviation industry is the creation of a more electric aircraft and in this case, there are no bleed systems that taking air from the engine, which is necessary to ensure the operation of the air conditioning system and ice protection system. This article discusses the possibility of using no bleed systems and calculating the required characteristics using mathematical modeling. Simulation results show the operation modes of a centrifugal compressor and using to compare two versions of the air-cooling units in case of rotational speed of compressor is limited. The simulation results presented in this article can be used in the design of compressors for advanced electric air conditioning systems.

articleTitle: Strength Check for a Solid Rocket Motor Shell based on Integrated Joint Simulation
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: Currently, the strength of the solid rocket motor shell is always checked without the consideration of the connecting blot and the nozzle, making the simulation cannot reproduce actual operating process to the full extent. In order to address the problem, this study adopted integrated joint simulation and checked the strength of a solid rocket motor shell under the operating condition with the maximum deviation, during which the nozzle and the connecting bolt were taken into account. Main conclusions are described below: The thermal insulation thickness of the nozzle satisfied the design requirement, and the temperature rise of the metal part at the outermost layer was only 2 K, i.e., the loss of strength induced by overheating can be avoided. The safety coefficient of the combustor shell was 1.46, which suggest that it was a reasonable design and can satisfy the operating requirement. The connecting bolt, the rear joint and the metal part of the nozzle were all at low stress level, with high safety coefficients. Accordingly, the structural integrity can be maintained during the operation.

articleTitle: Prediction of Remaining Engine Life Based on Multi-sensing Fusion
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: The stability and safety of the operation of an aero engine is very important for the flight of the aircraft, so its health status must be monitored at all times to ensure its safe operation. The traditional prediction algorithm for the remaining useful life (RUL) is often only shallow, and it is not possible to dig deep into the historical information of the sensor. Moreover, the traditional single sensor predicts the life, which often results in low or inefficient data utilization. Implementation issues. This paper presents a method for predicting remaining engine life based on multi-sense fusion. First, pre-process the data and extract, then, reconstruct the remaining sensor data through singular value decomposition (SVD); input the feature data into the deep GRU neural network for training to obtain the remaining engine life prediction Results; Finally, the commercial modular aero-propulsion system simulation (C-MAPSS) was selected for simulation experiments to verify the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Analysis and Modeling of Variable Cycle Engine Control System
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: Variable cycle engine (VCE) has many control variables, complex working process, wide range and fast change of environmental conditions, and complex control laws, which make the design of control system more difficult in engineering practice. In this paper, the double culvert VCE with core engine drive fan is studied. By analyzing the variation law of engine performance when the parameters of adjustable components change, the control quantity of the control system is determined. RSCN method is used to analyze and verify the rationality of the combination of different controlled quantities, and the controlled quantity of the control system is determined. The linear model of VCE is established and verified by simulation. The results show that the established linear model can accurately fit the nonlinear model, and the model linearization method is reasonable and effective, which can be used in the design of variable cycle engine control system.

articleTitle: Optimization of Aeroengine Robust Controller Based on Adaptive Simulated Annealing Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: In this paper, the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> robust controller is designed based on dual external variable cycle engine with core driven fan stage. The objective function is to calculate according to the performance requirements of the aeroengine control system, and the weight function matrix of the controller is optimized by the adaptive simulated annealing genetic algorithm. The H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> robust controller based on adaptive simulated annealing genetic algorithm for variable cycle engine is designed to avoid the drawbacks that the traditional method relies heavily on the designer's insufficient experience when selecting the weight function matrix, and solve the problem that it is time-consuming and laborious to select the weight function matrix through repeated tests. The simulation results of the nominal points and the selected points in the flight envelope show that this method can make the control system obtain better robust stability and robust performance, as well as strong anti-interference ability.

articleTitle: Aerodynamic Interference Optimization of the Fuselage-Pushing Propeller Configuration
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: Research on fuselage rational shapes and optimal volume to increase passenger capacity and to integrate the engine and airframe is an actual problem of air transport efficiency [1-3]. In order to experimentally study the operating conditions of the propeller in the aerodynamic wake, as well as to evaluate its effect on the total and distributed aerodynamic characteristics, a model fuselage was made, in the rear of which an electric motor was installed with a drive to the pusher propeller (Fig. 1) [4]. When choosing propeller parameters and designing, the six-bladed propeller models of different diameters were selected. As a result, the positive effect on the interaction with the pusher propeller was seen. The influence of the shape of rear fuselage on the thrust of propeller ring was investigated. Numerical calculation of the initial and modified shapes of fuselages with the propeller ring were performed with Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes equations on a structured mesh. The results showed that the change in the rear fuselage affected the local angle of attack at which the flow moves along the ring, and because of which the propeller thrust in the ring changed. It also increased both the surface pressure on the fuselage rear and the propeller thrust compared to the initial shape. In general, modifications to the rear fuselage improved thrust efficiency.

articleTitle: Parity-Space-Based FDI Approach for Advanced-Aeroengine Sensors
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: In this paper, a parity-space -based fault detection and isolation system for advanced turbofan engine sensors is proposed. The parity-space-based residual generator is constructed by using a parity vector, where the parity vector belongs to the parity space that is identified by using input/output data acquired from healthy aeroengine. These fault free aeroengine input/output data are stimulated by multi-sine signal inputs. Fault detection strategies and fault isolation strategies are proposed, which are designed according to robust principle. The schemes of aeroengine sensor fault detection and isolation system do not require a priori knowledge of the transfer matrix of linear model or the system order. The performance of the fault detection and isolation system is evaluated in a simulation environment at different operating points.

articleTitle: Engineering Algorithm and Verification of the Composite Stiffened Panel’S Compression Buckling
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: The finite element analysis simulation and engineering calculation of compression stability for T800 fiber-reinforced composite panel are performed. In the case of fixed end support and simple four-sided support, the influence of boundary conditions on the composite stiffened panel's buckling mode and buckling load are studied. Combined with the structural characteristics of the I-ribs, the engineering algorithm is made with six different boundary assumptions. Then the algorithm results are compared and verified with the results obtained by the finite element analysis. A method for selecting boundary conditions and calculating parameters for the I-ribs composite stiffened panel is presented, which is in good agreement with the finite element results.

articleTitle: Research on Cavitation Noise of a Balance Valve for Folding Boom Crane
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: The balance valve is an important hydraulic component. Sharp howling noise often occurs when a folding boom crane is operated. Aiming at the noise problem of the balance valve, a three-dimensional model of the internal flow field of the valve was established. Liquid-vapor two-phase flow simulations are performed under different inlet pressures and valve opening conditions. The generation and evolution of cavitation noise are revealed. Finally, an experiment under different inlet pressure conditions is carried out. Experimental results show that the cavitation noise is a periodic signal, mainly composed of 5 simple harmonic signals. As the inlet pressure increases, the noise at a certain frequency increases significantly. The research has a certain engineering practical significance for noise reduction of hydraulic valve.

articleTitle: Numerical Experiment of Flow Around a Compound Airfoil which Consists of Two Round Flat Plates
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: A numerical experiment around a compound airfoil which consists of two round flat plates was performed using the vortex method. The round flat plate is formed in the leading edge and the trailing edge by the semicircle which makes thickness of the plate a diameter. And application investigation was performed in order to use the plate as a rudder of a submarine. Movement speed was made into 1 knot (0.5 m/s) supposing a late velocity at the time of entry into port. The Reynolds number corresponding to the length (cord length C) and velocity of a plate was Re = 3.4x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>. In calculation, the angle of attack of a front round flat plate and a rear round flat plate was changed from 0 degree to 25 degrees, and a numerical simulation was performed. The time history of the fluid force of acting on the round flat plate, and the flow pattern were investigated. As a result of numerical experiment, the variation of flow pattern and the variation of fluid force which are based on changing an angle of attack were found.

articleTitle: Multiple Fault Diagnosis of Aeroengine Control System Based on Autoassociative Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: Aeroengine is a kind of complicated thermal machinery which works under high speed, high load and high temperature for a long time. In order to ensure the high reliability and stability of the engine, accurate and effective fault diagnosis is essential. The traditional model-based fault diagnosis method is difficult to achieve satisfactory results. The emergence of neural network intelligent algorithm provides a new idea. In order to obtain a fault diagnosis system with strong robustness and high detection rate, we design a the Autoassociative Neural Network (AANN) group to complete the detection and isolation of engine sensor faults and component faults, as well as the reconstruction of sensor faults. Firstly, the signal of the sensor of the aeroengine control system was preprocessed, and then a group of AANN network was designed according to the fault parameters for multiple fault detection and isolation of aeroengine. Finally, it was verified based on the MATLAB/Simulink platform. It is worth mentioning that this method does not require a model. It can be seen from simulation results that the proposed method can effectively reduce the noise of measurement data. Moreover, it has the advantages of fast diagnosis speed, strong robustness and synchronous detection and isolation. And it can effectively detect, isolate and reconstruct the faults of aeroengine.

articleTitle: A Comparison of ℋ∞-Synthesis and Feedback Linearization for Rotary Inverted Pendulum
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance comparison of ℋ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> based control and feedback linearization. The comparison is conducted on a challenging rotary inverted pendulum (RIP) system. The main difficulty of controlling RIP is the existence of RHP poles and zeros. Since the plant does not satisfy the typical ℋ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> control design conditions, a transformation of the location of RHP zeros is employed which put the system in a desired/solvable form. The existence of unstable internal dynamic states also causes some problems in the design of feedback linearization. These problems is solved by employing an outer loop cascade control scheme. The theoretical backgrounds and the design steps for the specific problem are listed. The designed controllers are tested on the nonlinear model whose parameters are perturbed to test the robustness of the controllers. The results of the Monte Carlo simulations are presented and findings are discussed.

articleTitle: Step-by-Step Longitudinal Aerodynamic Parameter Estimation Method for Fly-by-Wire Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: The fidelity of wind tunnel data often cannot meet the fidelity requirement of engineering simulator. Based on parameter decoupling principle, a step-by-step longitudinal parameter estimation method and a flight test procedure aiming at fly-by-wire aircraft was designed to avoid the disturb to estimation coming from the flight control system and decrease the collinearity of the flight data, as a result, improving the fidelity of estimation. The result of the parameter estimation reveals the response of dynamic model established on the basis of estimated parameter satisfied the tolerance of CCAR60, which means it meets the fidelity requirement of the engineering simulator. It also proves that the longitudinal parameter estimation method and the flight test procedure are capable of gaining a sound estimation.

articleTitle: A Quality Measurement Method For Maintenance of Space TT&C Software Based on Objective Data
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: Space TT&C software is the brain and central nervous system of the integrated space TT&C system of earth and sky. Its quality directly determines the success or failure of space launch TT&C mission. For each mission of the space TT&C software, application maintenance development needs to be performed on the software system accumulated over the years. The application maintenance process is closely integrated with the mission organization implementation process. According to the attributes of each stage of the application maintenance development process, the quality parameters are calculated based on the actual accumulated objective data, and then the stage quality assessment factors are determined. The proportion of each quality assessment factor is determined according to the degree of influence on the result. As the dual factors of efficiency and quality comprehensively considered, a quantitative measurement method for the maintenance quality of the space TT&C software based on objective data was established. The method can be used to evaluate the preparation status of the applied software before the implementation of the space TT&C mission.

articleTitle: Two Degree-of-Freedom μ Controller with Low Conservativeness for Aeroengine
publicationTitle: 2020 11th International Conference on Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (ICMAE)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of robustness and strong conservatism of traditional robust controllers for aeroengine. An improved on-board adaptive aeroengine model is designed to estimate engine performance degradation and the degradation term in the engine uncertain models is eliminated. On the basis of the traditional μ controller, a pre-filter and a feedback controller are added. By adjusting the feedback controller, the transfer function of the interference to the output meets the requirements, that is, the ability of disturbance suppression is optimal. On this basis, the pre-filter is adjusted to make the transfer function of reference input-to-output meets the requirements, that is, the system's tracking ability reaches the best. The two degree-of-freedom μ controller with low conservativeness for aeroengine is developed. The developed control scheme can guarantee that the closed-loop system is robust stable. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the presented control scheme.
